library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

Li 2014 built a modular mechanistic model of influenza A virus (IAV) infection
in humans and used it to ask whether oseltamivir and amantadine act
synergistically. Two versions were fitted and compared throughout the paper,
and both are packaged:

* `Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_qsp` -- the full model with innate (IFN-alpha)
  and cell-mediated adaptive (CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte) immune responses,
  the paper's "+IM" model.
* `Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_noimmune_qsp` -- the target-cell-limited model
  without immune responses, the paper's "-IM" model.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_qsp"))$reference`
* Description (+IM): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_qsp"))$description`
* Description (-IM): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_noimmune_qsp"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2014.32> (open access, with the
  supplementary equations, parameter tables and model code)

```{r models}
mod_im <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_qsp"))
mod_noim <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2014_oseltamivir_amantadine_noimmune_qsp"))
```

# Population

The model describes a single typical ("average") adult. Li 2014 did not fit
individual data; each module was calibrated against published summary data:

* PK modules (Figure 2): a 150 + 75 mg oseltamivir loading-dose multidose study
  in Thai volunteers (Wattanagoon 2009), a 150 mg single dose in Japanese and
  Caucasian volunteers (Jhee 2008), amantadine 100 mg once daily (Reuman 1989)
  and a 200 mg amantadine single dose averaged over young and elderly adults
  (Hayden 1985). Clearances and volumes are for a 70-kg adult.
* Immune modules (Figure 3): nasal-lavage viral titre and IFN-alpha after
  experimental human IAV infection (Hayden 1998).
* Treatment (Figure 4): oseltamivir 75 and 150 mg twice daily versus placebo
  (Treanor 2000) and amantadine versus placebo (Knight 1970).

Parameters were estimated with a genetic algorithm (GAPSM) inside
literature-based ranges (Supplementary Table S2). The model carries no
between-subject variability and no residual error.

```{r population}
str(mod_im$population)
```

# Source trace

Equations are from Supplementary Table S1, parameter values from Supplementary
Table S2 (where a parameter differs between the models the table prints the
+IM value first and the -IM value second), and initial values from
Supplementary Table S3. Paper parameter K numbers are kept in each `label()`.

| Parameter (paper name) | +IM | -IM | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lktr` (K1a, OP dissolution delay) | log(6.412) 1/h | same | Table S2 |
| `lka` (K1b, OP absorption) | log(0.3652) 1/h | same | Table S2 |
| `lkm` (K2, OP to OC conversion) | log(1.768) 1/h | same | Table S2 |
| `lcl` / `lvc` (CLOP / VDOP) | log(78060) mL/h / log(212600) mL | same | Table S2 |
| `lcl_oselcarb` / `lvc_oselcarb` (CLOC / VDOC) | log(26460) mL/h / log(115000) mL | same | Table S2 |
| `lktr_amantadine` (K19, AMT dissolution delay) | log(62.69) 1/h | same | Table S2 |
| `lka_amantadine` (K20, AMT absorption) | log(3.356) 1/h | same | Table S2 |
| `lcl_amantadine` / `lvc_amantadine` (CLAMT / VDAMT) | log(12850) mL/h / log(325900) mL | same | Table S2 |
| `lic50_oselcarb` (1/K17) | log(1/0.0445) ng/mL | log(1/0.0237) | Table S2; Table S1 footnote d |
| `lic50_amantadine` (1/K22) | log(1/0.07987) ng/mL | log(1/0.25710) | Table S2; Table S1 footnote b |
| `lbeta` (K11, epithelial infection) | log(1.04e-5) | log(4.74e-6) | Table S2 |
| `lk_eclipse` (K13, eclipse transition) | log(0.06191) 1/h | log(0.11661) | Table S2 |
| `ldelta` (K14, infected-cell death) | log(0.4196) 1/h | log(0.35438) | Table S2 |
| `lp_virus` (K16, virus release) | log(0.00231) | log(0.000933) | Table S2 |
| `lc_virus` (K18, virus elimination) | log(0.6007) 1/h | log(0.31658) | Table S2 |
| `lk_ifn_ctl` (K24) | log(0.01439) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lkdeg_ifn` (K25) | log(1.856) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_protect` (K26) | log(0.0003995) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_revert` (K27) | log(8.066e-5) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_nk` (K28) | log(1.614e-7) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_ctl_act` (K32) | log(0.1135) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_ctl_kill` (K34) | log(5.002e-6) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_apc_mig` (K37) | log(0.111) 1/h | -- | **not tabulated**; back-solved from Figure 3a (below) |
| `lkdeg_apc_act` (K42) | log(0.07744) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `lkdeg_ctl` (K45) | log(0.04555) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_ifn_inf` (K47) | log(5.45e-14) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_apc_inf` (K48) | log(0.004715) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lkdeg_apc_inf` (K53) | log(0.09598) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_ifn_apc` (K57) | log(0.01177) | -- | Table S2 |
| `lk_apc_turn` (K59) | log(6.459e-7) 1/h | -- | Table S2 |
| `f_ctl_lung` | fixed(0.15) | -- | Methods; Table S1 footnote c |
| `tau_ctl_mig` / `tau_apc_mig` | fixed(12) h / fixed(24) h | -- | Methods; Table S1 footnotes c, f |
| `apc0` | fixed(1e5) cells | -- | Methods; Table S1; Table S3 |
| `target0` | fixed(4e8) cells | same | Table S3 |
| `virus0` | fixed(10) TCID50/mL | same | Methods 'Calculation of synergy'; per-figure values in Table S3 |
| PK ODEs | -- | -- | Table S1 'PK Modules' |
| Virus life-cycle and immune ODEs | -- | -- | Table S1 (with / without immune systems) |
| Delayed terms `delay(ctl, 12)`, `delay(apc_infected, 24)` | -- | -- | Table S1 footnotes c, f; authors' `delaymodelfun.R` |
| `log10_viral_load = log10(virus + 1)` | -- | -- | Table S3 note (pseudo count of 1) |

# Helpers

All solves below are typical-value solves of a single subject. The +IM model
contains delay differential equations, so it is solved with `dop853` and a large
step budget.

```{r helpers}
solve_im <- function(events, params = NULL) {
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_im, events = events, params = params,
                         method = "dop853", maxsteps = 1e7,
                         returnType = "data.frame")
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- 1L
  out
}
solve_noim <- function(events, params = NULL) {
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_noim, events = events, params = params,
                         returnType = "data.frame")
  if (is.null(out$id)) out$id <- 1L
  out
}
# Twice-daily oral dosing of OP and/or AMT starting at `t_first` h, with
# observations on a fixed grid.
bid_events <- function(op_mg, amt_mg, t_first, n_doses, obs_times) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(obs_times)
  if (op_mg > 0) {
    ev <- ev |> rxode2::et(amt = op_mg, cmt = "depot", time = t_first,
                           ii = 12, addl = n_doses - 1)
  }
  if (amt_mg > 0) {
    ev <- ev |> rxode2::et(amt = amt_mg, cmt = "depot_amantadine",
                           time = t_first, ii = 12, addl = n_doses - 1)
  }
  ev
}
value_at <- function(sim, var, t) {
  v <- sim[[var]][match(t, sim$time)]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(v))
  v
}
```

# PK modules (Figure 2)

The PK modules are shared by both models; the +IM model is used here. Panel a
gives the oseltamivir loading-dose regimen (150 mg then 75 mg twice daily) and
a 150 mg single dose; panel b gives amantadine 100 mg once daily and a 200 mg
single dose.

```{r figure-2}
pk_scen <- list(
  "a-left: OP 150 + 75 mg q12h" = rxode2::et(c(seq(0, 24, 0.25), seq(25, 48, 1))) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 150, cmt = "depot", time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 75, cmt = "depot", time = 12, ii = 12, addl = 2),
  # Sampled to 72 h (Figure 2 shows 24 h) so that the PKNCA terminal phase
  # below is clear of the absorption phase (OP ka 0.37/h vs OC kel 0.23/h).
  "a-right: OP 150 mg single" = rxode2::et(seq(0, 72, 0.25)) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 150, cmt = "depot", time = 0),
  "b-left: AMT 100 mg q24h" = rxode2::et(seq(0, 168, 0.5)) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 100, cmt = "depot_amantadine", time = 0, ii = 24, addl = 6),
  "b-right: AMT 200 mg single" = rxode2::et(seq(0, 72, 0.25)) |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 200, cmt = "depot_amantadine", time = 0)
)
pk_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pk_scen), function(nm) {
  solve_im(pk_scen[[nm]], params = c(virus0 = 0)) |>
    mutate(panel = nm)
}))
pk_long <- pk_sim |>
  select(panel, time, OP = Cc, OC = Cc_oselcarb, AMT = Cc_amantadine) |>
  pivot_longer(c(OP, OC, AMT), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter((grepl("^a", panel) & analyte != "AMT") | (grepl("^b", panel) & analyte == "AMT"))
ggplot(pk_long, aes(time, conc, linetype = analyte)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       linetype = NULL, caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Li 2014.")
```

The simulated curves match the drawn model lines of Figure 2: an OC peak of
about 480 ng/mL near 4 h and an OP peak near 80 ng/mL after 150 mg, a first
amantadine peak near 290 ng/mL after 100 mg, and an amantadine peak near
580 ng/mL with about 35 ng/mL remaining at 72 h after 200 mg.

```{r figure-2-check}
s150 <- pk_sim |> filter(panel == "a-right: OP 150 mg single")
s200 <- pk_sim |> filter(panel == "b-right: AMT 200 mg single")
s100 <- pk_sim |> filter(panel == "b-left: AMT 100 mg q24h")
fig2 <- tibble(
  quantity = c("OC Cmax, OP 150 mg (ng/mL)", "OC Tmax, OP 150 mg (h)",
               "OP Cmax, OP 150 mg (ng/mL)", "AMT Cmax, 200 mg (ng/mL)",
               "AMT C72, 200 mg (ng/mL)", "AMT first-dose Cmax, 100 mg (ng/mL)"),
  figure = c(480, 4, 80, 580, 35, 290),
  simulated = c(max(s150$Cc_oselcarb), s150$time[which.max(s150$Cc_oselcarb)],
                max(s150$Cc), max(s200$Cc_amantadine), value_at(s200, "Cc_amantadine", 72),
                max(s100$Cc_amantadine[s100$time < 24]))
)
knitr::kable(fig2, digits = 1)
# Deterministic solve against values read off the drawn model line; the
# tolerance covers reading precision on the printed figure.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig2$simulated / fig2$figure - 1) < 0.15))
```

## PKNCA

Li 2014 reports no NCA table; the single-dose NCA below documents the exposure
the PK modules imply.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- bind_rows(
  s150 |> transmute(id = 1L, time, conc = Cc_oselcarb, treatment = "OC after OP 150 mg"),
  s150 |> transmute(id = 1L, time, conc = Cc, treatment = "OP after OP 150 mg"),
  s200 |> transmute(id = 1L, time, conc = Cc_amantadine, treatment = "AMT 200 mg")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(conc))
nca_dose <- tibble(
  id = 1L, time = 0,
  dose = c(150, 150, 200),
  treatment = c("OC after OP 150 mg", "OP after OP 150 mg", "AMT 200 mg")
)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Analyte / regimen" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax,
                "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-inf (h*ng/mL)" = aucinf.obs,
                "t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The amantadine half-life equals `log(2) * VDAMT / CLAMT` =
`r round(log(2) * 325900 / 12850, 1)` h, and the OC terminal half-life equals
`log(2) * VDOC / CLOC` = `r round(log(2) * 115000 / 26460, 1)` h, as a
one-compartment module requires.

```{r pknca-check}
hl <- setNames(nca_tab$half.life, nca_tab$treatment)
stopifnot(
  abs(hl[["AMT 200 mg"]] / (log(2) * 325900 / 12850) - 1) < 0.02,
  abs(hl[["OC after OP 150 mg"]] / (log(2) * 115000 / 26460) - 1) < 0.02
)
```

# Immune response after infection (Figure 3)

Figure 3 simulates an untreated experimental infection with the +IM model,
starting from the Table S3 initial titre of 1.474e-5 TCID50/mL. The circles
are the nasal-lavage titres and IFN-alpha levels of Hayden 1998 as given in
the authors' supplementary data file (titres shown, as in the paper, as
log10(titre + 1)).

```{r figure-3-data}
fig3_obs <- tibble(
  time = c(0, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168, 192),
  log10_titre = c(NA, 1.865, 3.752, 3.329, 2.613, 2.484, 1.305, 0.857, 0.364),
  ifna = c(0, 6.03, 157.4, 20.3, 47.8, 57.9, 19.3, 2.8, 0)
)
# Model line of Figure 3a read at the 24-h grid on which it is drawn.
fig3_line <- tibble(
  time = c(0, 24, 48, 72, 96, 120, 144, 168, 192),
  log10_titre = c(0, 0.25, 3.75, 4.0, 3.15, 2.05, 1.35, 0.68, 0.35),
  ifna = c(0, 5, 157, 20, 80, 57, 20, 5, 1)
)
```

## Back-solving K37

The Table S1 equation for activated lymph-node APC,
`d(ActivatedAPCLymphnode)/dt = K37*InfectedAPC(t-24) - K42*ActivatedAPCLymphnode`,
uses a rate constant K37 that has no row in Table S2 (the authors' example
code carries a placeholder value, and none of that code's values are the final
estimates). Activated APC feed only CTL production, so every model output
depends on K37 only through the product K32 * K37; with K32 fixed at its
printed value the remaining factor is identified by the paper's own simulated
curves. The maintainers fitted K37 by least squares to the drawn model line of
Figure 3a (titre on the log10 scale; IFN-alpha scaled by 40 pg/mL):

```{r k37-backsolve}
fig3_events <- rxode2::et(sort(unique(c(seq(0, 192, 0.5)))))
k37_loss <- function(k37) {
  s <- solve_im(fig3_events, params = c(virus0 = 1.474e-5, lk_apc_mig = log(k37)))
  sum((value_at(s, "log10_viral_load", fig3_line$time) - fig3_line$log10_titre)^2) +
    sum(((value_at(s, "ifna", fig3_line$time) - fig3_line$ifna) / 40)^2)
}
k37_fit <- optimize(k37_loss, c(0.03, 0.3), tol = 1e-3)
k37_fit$minimum
stopifnot(abs(k37_fit$minimum - 0.111) < 0.005)
```

The fitted value, 0.111 1/h, is the packaged `lk_apc_mig`. Two features of the
paper that did not enter the fit confirm it: the ratio of the second to the
first IFN-alpha peak in Figure 3b (about 0.19 by eye) and the +IM curves of
Figure 4 below.

```{r figure-3}
fig3_sim <- solve_im(fig3_events, params = c(virus0 = 1.474e-5))
bind_rows(
  fig3_sim |> transmute(time, value = log10_viral_load, panel = "Viral titre, log10(TCID50/mL + 1)"),
  fig3_sim |> transmute(time, value = ifna, panel = "Nasal IFN-alpha (pg/mL)")
) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = bind_rows(
    fig3_obs |> transmute(time, value = log10_titre, panel = "Viral titre, log10(TCID50/mL + 1)"),
    fig3_obs |> transmute(time, value = ifna, panel = "Nasal IFN-alpha (pg/mL)")
  ), shape = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time post infection (h)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Li 2014.")
```

```{r figure-3b}
fig3_sim |>
  mutate(ctl_lung = 0.15 * lag(ctl, 24)) |>
  transmute(time, `Infected APC` = apc_infected / max(apc_infected),
            `IFN-alpha` = ifna / max(ifna),
            `Cytotoxic T cells (lung)` = ctl_lung / max(ctl_lung, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pivot_longer(-time) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, linetype = name)) +
  geom_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Time post infection (h)", y = "Fraction of maximum amount", linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3b of Li 2014. Lung CTL: 0.15 x lymph-node CTL 12 h earlier.")
```

```{r figure-3-check}
early <- fig3_sim$time < 60
fig3_check <- tibble(
  quantity = c("infected-APC peak time (h)", "first IFN-alpha peak time (h)",
               "second IFN-alpha peak time (h)", "IFN-alpha second / first peak",
               "lung CTL peak time (h)"),
  figure = c(37, 37, 97, 0.19, 97),
  simulated = c(fig3_sim$time[which.max(fig3_sim$apc_infected)],
                fig3_sim$time[early][which.max(fig3_sim$ifna[early])],
                fig3_sim$time[!early][which.max(fig3_sim$ifna[!early])],
                max(fig3_sim$ifna[!early]) / max(fig3_sim$ifna[early]),
                fig3_sim$time[which.max(fig3_sim$ctl)] + 12)
)
knitr::kable(fig3_check, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(value_at(fig3_sim, "log10_viral_load", fig3_line$time) - fig3_line$log10_titre) < 0.3),
  abs(value_at(fig3_sim, "ifna", 48) / 157 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(fig3_check$simulated[4] - 0.19) < 0.03,
  all(abs(fig3_check$simulated[-4] - fig3_check$figure[-4]) <= 3)
)
```

# Monotherapy with and without immune responses (Figure 4)

Li 2014 draws its model lines in Figures 3 and 4 by joining the simulated
values at the data times only (a straight line from infection to 96 h, for
example), so the continuous curves below agree with the published lines at the
data times but not necessarily in between. The Figure 4a points are digitised
from the figure; the Figure 4b points are from the authors' supplementary data
file.

Treatment starts 96 h after infection (Methods). The initial titre of each
group was fitted separately by Li 2014 and is taken from Table S3. Figure 4a is
oseltamivir 75 or 150 mg twice daily (Treanor 2000); Figure 4b is amantadine
100 mg twice daily (Knight 1970).

```{r figure-4-scenarios}
fig4_scen <- tribble(
  ~panel, ~arm, ~op, ~amt, ~v0_im, ~v0_noim,
  "a", "Placebo", 0, 0, 4.136e-7, 0.03996,
  "a", "OP 75 mg", 75, 0, 1.849e-7, 0.02006,
  "a", "OP 150 mg", 150, 0, 2.486e-6, 0.1098,
  "b", "Placebo", 0, 0, 5.541e-9, 5.686e-4,
  "b", "AMT 100 mg", 0, 100, 1.005e-10, 0.001157
)
fig4_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig4_scen)), function(i) {
  sc <- fig4_scen[i, ]
  t_end <- if (sc$panel == "a") 168 else 178
  ev <- bid_events(sc$op, sc$amt, t_first = 96, n_doses = 10, obs_times = seq(0, t_end, 1))
  bind_rows(
    solve_im(ev, params = c(virus0 = sc$v0_im)) |> mutate(model = "+IM"),
    solve_noim(ev, params = c(virus0 = sc$v0_noim)) |> mutate(model = "-IM")
  ) |>
    mutate(panel = sc$panel, arm = sc$arm)
}))
fig4_obs <- tribble(
  ~panel, ~arm, ~time, ~log10_titre,
  "a", "Placebo", 96, 3.50, "a", "Placebo", 120, 2.30, "a", "Placebo", 168, 0.30,
  "a", "OP 75 mg", 96, 3.50, "a", "OP 75 mg", 120, 1.80, "a", "OP 75 mg", 168, 0.30,
  "a", "OP 150 mg", 96, 3.35, "a", "OP 150 mg", 120, 1.30, "a", "OP 150 mg", 168, 0.30,
  "b", "Placebo", 96, 3.97, "b", "Placebo", 106, 3.28, "b", "Placebo", 130, 1.95,
  "b", "Placebo", 154, 1.54, "b", "Placebo", 178, 1.16,
  "b", "AMT 100 mg", 96, 4.46, "b", "AMT 100 mg", 106, 2.50, "b", "AMT 100 mg", 130, 1.78,
  "b", "AMT 100 mg", 154, 1.41, "b", "AMT 100 mg", 178, 1.11
)
```

```{r figure-4ab, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(fig4_sim, aes(time, log10_viral_load, linetype = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = fig4_obs, aes(time, log10_titre, shape = arm)) +
  facet_grid(panel ~ model) +
  labs(x = "Time post infection (h)", y = "Viral titre, log10(TCID50/mL + 1)",
       linetype = NULL, shape = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4a (top) and 4b (bottom) of Li 2014.")
```

```{r figure-4c}
fig4_sim |>
  filter(panel == "b", arm == "Placebo") |>
  select(model, time, `Viral titre (log10)` = log10_viral_load,
         `Fraction uninfected` = frac_uninfected) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(model, time)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(name ~ model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time post infection (h)", y = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4c of Li 2014 (placebo course of Figure 4b).")
```

The -IM model depletes essentially every target cell by the time of peak
titre, while the +IM model leaves about 87% of the epithelium uninfected (or
IFN-protected) throughout -- the contrast Li 2014 draws in Figure 4c.

```{r figure-4-check}
# Drawn model lines of Figure 4 read at the plotted data times.
fig4_line <- tribble(
  ~model, ~panel, ~arm, ~time, ~line,
  "-IM", "a", "Placebo", 120, 2.3, "-IM", "a", "Placebo", 168, 0.2,
  "-IM", "a", "OP 75 mg", 120, 1.7, "-IM", "a", "OP 150 mg", 120, 1.3,
  "+IM", "a", "Placebo", 120, 2.35, "+IM", "a", "Placebo", 168, 0.8,
  "+IM", "a", "OP 75 mg", 120, 1.7, "+IM", "a", "OP 150 mg", 120, 1.2,
  "-IM", "b", "Placebo", 96, 4.05, "-IM", "b", "Placebo", 178, 0.3,
  "-IM", "b", "AMT 100 mg", 178, 1.35,
  "+IM", "b", "Placebo", 96, 3.8, "+IM", "b", "Placebo", 178, 0.8,
  "+IM", "b", "AMT 100 mg", 178, 1.1
)
fig4_cmp <- fig4_line |>
  left_join(fig4_sim |> select(model, panel, arm, time, simulated = log10_viral_load),
            by = c("model", "panel", "arm", "time"))
knitr::kable(fig4_cmp, digits = 2)
fu <- fig4_sim |> filter(panel == "b", arm == "Placebo")
stopifnot(
  nrow(fig4_cmp) == nrow(fig4_line), !anyNA(fig4_cmp$simulated),
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$simulated - fig4_cmp$line) < 0.3),
  value_at(fu |> filter(model == "-IM"), "frac_uninfected", 96) < 0.01,
  abs(value_at(fu |> filter(model == "+IM"), "frac_uninfected", 178) - 0.87) < 0.05
)
```

# Drug-combination synergy (Figure 5)

Li 2014 scored synergy with the Prichard and Shipman method: with X, Y and E
the fractional inhibitions of viral titre by OP alone, AMT alone and the
combination, the additive expectation is `Z = X + Y(1 - X)` and synergy is
`S = E - Z` (in percent). Per the Methods, the initial titre was fixed at 10,
the first dose was given 96 h after infection, doses were twice daily, and
inhibition was read 24 h after the first dose relative to placebo. Resistant
strains multiply the corresponding in vivo IC50 by 10.

Two details are not stated: the titre scale on which inhibition was computed
and the exact dose grid. On the linear titre scale S stays close to zero
everywhere (column `max |S| linear` below), which cannot produce the surfaces of
Figure 5, so inhibition is computed on the log10(titre + 1) scale that every
other figure of the paper uses. A coarse 5 x 5 dose grid keeps the render
short.

```{r synergy, fig.height = 8}
synergy_grid <- function(model, doses_op, doses_amt, fold_op, fold_amt) {
  grid <- expand.grid(op = doses_op, amt = doses_amt)
  base_p <- c(virus0 = 10)
  if (model == "+IM") {
    base_p <- c(base_p, lic50_oselcarb = log(fold_op / 0.0445),
                lic50_amantadine = log(fold_amt / 0.07987))
  } else {
    base_p <- c(base_p, lic50_oselcarb = log(fold_op / 0.0237),
                lic50_amantadine = log(fold_amt / 0.25710))
  }
  grid$virus <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
    ev <- bid_events(grid$op[i], grid$amt[i], t_first = 96, n_doses = 2, obs_times = c(0, 120))
    s <- if (model == "+IM") solve_im(ev, params = base_p) else solve_noim(ev, params = base_p)
    value_at(s, "virus", 120)
  }, numeric(1))
  grid$S <- prichard_shipman(grid, log10(grid$virus + 1))
  grid$S_linear <- prichard_shipman(grid, grid$virus)
  grid
}
# S = E - (X + Y(1 - X)), in percent, from the titre on a given scale; the
# single-drug rows (amt == 0, op == 0) supply X and Y.
prichard_shipman <- function(grid, titre) {
  key <- paste(grid$op, grid$amt)
  inhib <- 1 - titre / titre[key == "0 0"]
  x <- inhib[match(paste(grid$op, 0), key)]
  y <- inhib[match(paste(0, grid$amt), key)]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(x), !anyNA(y))
  100 * (inhib - (x + y * (1 - x)))
}
strains <- tribble(
  ~strain, ~fold_op, ~fold_amt, ~dmax,
  "a: wild type", 1, 1, 100,
  "b: AMT resistant", 1, 10, 400,
  "c: OP resistant", 10, 1, 400,
  "d: double resistant", 10, 10, 400
)
syn <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(strains)), function(i) {
  st <- strains[i, ]
  doses <- seq(0, st$dmax, length.out = 5)
  bind_rows(lapply(c("-IM", "+IM"), function(m) {
    synergy_grid(m, doses, doses, st$fold_op, st$fold_amt) |>
      mutate(model = m, strain = st$strain)
  }))
}))
ggplot(syn, aes(op, amt, fill = S)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue", mid = "white", high = "orchid4", midpoint = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ strain + model, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "OP dose (mg, twice daily)", y = "AMT dose (mg, twice daily)", fill = "S (%)",
       caption = "Compare Figure 5 of Li 2014 (coarse grid; see text).")
```

```{r synergy-summary}
syn_summary <- syn |>
  filter(op > 0, amt > 0) |>
  group_by(strain, model) |>
  summarise(`mean S` = mean(S), `max S` = max(S),
            `max |S| linear` = max(abs(S_linear)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(syn_summary, digits = 1)
# Deterministic solves: pin the wild-type summary so a change to either model
# shows up here.
wt <- syn_summary |> filter(strain == "a: wild type")
stopifnot(
  nrow(wt) == 2, nrow(syn) == 8 * 25,
  abs(wt$`mean S`[wt$model == "+IM"] - 5.9) < 0.3,
  abs(wt$`mean S`[wt$model == "-IM"] - 5.3) < 0.3,
  all(syn_summary$`max |S| linear` < 2.5)
)
```

Under this reading of the protocol synergy is positive over most of the grid
for both models, and the +IM model predicts somewhat more synergy than the -IM
model for the wild-type, OP-resistant and double-resistant strains. The gap is
much smaller than in Figure 5, however, and it reverses for the AMT-resistant
strain, so **the packaged models do not reproduce Figure 5**. The synergy
protocol is not specified completely (the dose grid, the time origin of the
synergy runs and the inhibition scale), and the authors' synergy script is not
among the supplementary files. Figures 2 to 4, which fix every model parameter,
are reproduced closely, so the difference most likely lies in the synergy
protocol rather than in the models; it has not been resolved.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **K37 back-solved.** The APC migration/activation rate constant K37 appears in
  the Table S1 equations but not in Table S2 or anywhere else in the paper or
  supplements. It was back-solved by the maintainers from the drawn model curve
  of Figure 3a (0.111 1/h) and is consistent with Figures 3b and 4. Only the
  product K32 * K37 is identifiable, so splitting it differently would give
  identical predictions.
* **Drug-to-parameter mapping.** The Methods say resistance multiplies "the in
  vivo IC50 (inverse of K17 for AMT and K22 for OC respectively)". Table S1
  (footnotes b and d), Table S2 and the authors' code all pair K17 with OC and
  K22 with AMT; the packaged model follows the tables and code.
* **Figure 4b dose.** The Figure 4 caption says amantadine 150 mg twice daily,
  but the authors' data file doses 100 mg every 12 h from 96 h, and 100 mg
  reproduces the drawn Figure 4b curves while 150 mg does not; 100 mg is used.
  Table S3 labels the third Figure 4a initial titre "100 mg group"; Figure 4a
  has a 150 mg group, which is the group it is used for here.
* **Units.** Table S2 lists the infection-rate units of K11 and K48 per log10
  TCID50/mL, but the equations and the authors' code use the linear titre;
  the linear titre is used. Drug concentrations are amounts in mg over volumes
  in mL, converted to ng/mL to match K17 and K22. The OP-to-OC conversion
  carries no molecular-weight correction, as printed.
* **IL-6.** The authors' example code carries an IL-6 state that feeds back on
  nothing and is absent from the Table S1 equations; it is omitted.
* **Initial titre.** `virus0` defaults to the value 10 that the paper used for
  its drug-combination simulations; the per-figure titres of Table S3 are
  passed as parameter overrides above.
* **Figure 5 not reproduced.** The synergy surfaces computed above under the
  stated protocol (initial titre 10, first dose at 96 h, inhibition 24 h later
  on the log10 titre scale) are positive but flatter than Figure 5, and the
  +IM model's advantage is small; see the Figure 5 section.
* **No variability.** Li 2014 adopts typical values only, so neither model has
  between-subject variability or residual error.
